/-!
# Conjecture 8.24

by V. M. Kopytov

Prove that every linearly ordered group of finite rank is soluble.

A *linearly ordered group* is a group $G$ with a total order $\le$ that is invariant under
multiplication on both sides: $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and $ac \le bc$ for all
$a, b, c \in G$. Mathlib's ordered-group classes (`IsOrderedMonoid`, `LinearOrderedCommGroup`)
are commutative, so the (not necessarily commutative) two-sided invariant total order is encoded
by `[Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G]`.

The *rank* of $G$ is the special rank of Mal'cev (also called the Prüfer rank): $G$ has finite
rank if there is an $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be
generated by at most $r$ elements.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 8.24
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified claim (∀ G, G a group with a bi-invariant (two-sided) total order and of finite rank → IsSolvable G); 'rank' here is the Mal'cev special/Prüfer rank (∃ r, every finitely generated subgroup is generated by ≤ r elements) — not Mathlib's `Group.rank`, which needs `Group.FG` — and Mathlib's ordered-group classes (`IsOrderedMonoid`, `LinearOrderedCommGroup`) are commutative-only, so the noncommutative order must be encoded via `[Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G]` or an equivalent.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition: G a group with a total order invariant under left and right multiplication ([Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G]; verified these give c*a ≤ c*b and a*c ≤ b*c), finite Mal'cev special/Prüfer rank, conclusion IsSolvable G (finite derived length). The rank encodings are provably equivalent: c01/c02 use `∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r` (Group.rank = Nat.find of min generating-set size; Group.fg_iff_subgroup_fg links the instance to H.FG), c03/c06 use a Finset in the subtype ↥H with closure = ⊤, c04/c05/c08 use a Finset of G with closure = H, c07 wraps the latter in a bespoke def plus a test. I chose c05's inline elementary form (most transparent, no bespoke definition needed for a one-line predicate, universe-polymorphic `Type*` binder rather than `∀ G : Type`, AMS 6 20 in ascending order, good docstrings) and expanded the module docstring to explain the two encoding choices as in c01. The file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; the hypotheses are satisfiable (Multiplicative ℤ, checked) and non-trivial (free groups are bi-orderable, non-soluble, of infinite rank).

namespace Kourovka.«8.24»

/--
Prove that every linearly ordered group of finite rank is soluble.

Here $G$ is a group with a total order $\le$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ and
$ac \le bc$ for all $c \in G$ (`MulLeftMono G` and `MulRightMono G`). Finite rank means finite
Mal'cev special (Prüfer) rank: there is an $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every finitely generated
subgroup of $G$ is generated by a set of at most $r$ elements.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.24» (G : Type*) [Group G] [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G]
    (hrank : ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
      ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = H) :
    IsSolvable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.24»

items: 'Linearly ordered group' is read in the standard (Kokorin–Kopytov) sense of a two-sided ordered group: `LinearOrder G` with `MulLeftMono G` and `MulRightMono G`. Mathlib's `IsOrderedMonoid`/`LinearOrderedCommGroup` require commutativity, so the unbundled covariant classes are used. Strict monotonicity (`MulLeftStrictMono`, `MulRightStrictMono`) follows automatically in a group, so it is not assumed separately.

'Finite rank' is read as Mal'cev's special (Prüfer) rank, per the decomposition table: ∃ r, every finitely generated subgroup is generated by ≤ r elements. It is written elementarily (`H.FG → ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure S = H`) rather than via `Group.rank ↥H ≤ r`, because `Group.rank` needs a `Group.FG ↥H` instance for each subgroup; the two formulations are equivalent. Other readings of 'rank' (e.g. torsion-free/Hirsch rank, abelian section rank) were not used.
'Soluble' is Mathlib's `IsSolvable G` (derived series reaches ⊥ in finitely many steps), not locally soluble or hyperabelian.
The problem is phrased as 'Prove that …', so it is stated as a plain theorem `P` without `answer(sorry)`, following CONTRIBUTING.md.

The group is quantified with `(G : Type*)` as a theorem binder (rather than `∀ (G : Type)` inside the statement) since the claim is not a yes/no question; this is universe-polymorphic and matches the repository's plain-theorem style.
Boundary case: `r = 0` forces `G` to be trivial (hence solvable); the hypotheses are satisfiable (e.g. `Multiplicative ℤ`), so the statement is not vacuous.
AMS tags 6 (ordered algebraic structures) and 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: 'rank' is unqualified. Following the decomposition table and all candidates, it is read as Mal'cev's special (Prüfer) rank — the standard meaning of 'group of finite rank' in the Kourovka Notebook / Novosibirsk school. The alternative order-theoretic reading (finitely many convex subgroups) would make the statement an easy theorem (each convex jump C ≺ D has C normal in D with D/C Archimedean hence abelian by Hölder), so it cannot be the intended open problem; torsion-free/Hirsch rank is not defined for general groups. 'Linearly ordered group' is read as a two-sided (bi-invariant) total order, Kopytov's standard usage (right-ordered groups are a different notion in his terminology). 'Soluble' is Mathlib's IsSolvable (finite derived length), not local solubility. The problem is imperative ('Prove that ...'), so no answer(sorry) is used, per CONTRIBUTING.md. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised by any candidate, and I agree with the table. Only style differences between candidates: Type vs Type*, Group.rank vs inline Finset form, bespoke def (c07). c07's HasFiniteSpecialRank is a generic notion that per CONTRIBUTING would belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib rather than the problem file, so the inline form was preferred.
statement: Prove that every linearly ordered group of finite rank is soluble.
